label: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017
output:
Good day Mr Kehinde Ogunleye,

I hope you are doing well. My name is [Your Name]. I am the student whose black Jansport bag you found in the danfo on Friday, 6 November, on the Oshodi–Igando route. I came down at Ikotun. Thank you again for calling the number on my lab manual. Honestly, many people would have thrown that bag away or ignored it, so I do not take what you did for granted.

I am writing about getting the bag back. When we spoke, you mentioned ₦40,000. I have to be honest with you, sir: I cannot raise that amount. I am a first-year Biology student and that is far beyond what I have. The bag contained my lab manual, dissecting kit, student ID, two textbooks, calculator and my glasses, but the whole bag and books do not come close to ₦40,000. My practical is on Wednesday, 11 November at 10am, and without the dissecting kit there is no entry. The lab attendant is very strict, so this is really urgent for me.

I can manage ₦10,000 for your transport and as a thank-you. That is all my allowance. I am offering it sincerely, not to insult you. I’m not a mugu and I’m not trying to play games with you; I’m just telling you the truth about what I can afford. Please help me with this.

My roommate Adaeze can follow me so it is not awkward. We can meet in the daytime at a public place. Ikotun Roundabout or the area by the Ikotun Police Division gate are both open, public places I know, but please choose whichever is convenient and safe for you. Kindly pick a day before Wednesday so I can collect the bag and prepare for my practical.

Please reply and let me know what you decide. Thank you, sir.

[Your Name]
[Your Phone Number]
